In practice, it is applied to rendered feature maps with a dimension of 128 to align with higher-dimensional targets (e.g., 256 or 512) [S2].

The evidence explicitly states in the 'Training and Inference Details' section: 'In practice, we use the Speed-up Module with the rendered feature dim = 128.' It further explains that the Speed-up Module's objective is to 'modify the feature map channels, enabling the relatively low-dimensional semantic features rendered from 3D Gaussians to align with the high-dimensional ground truth 2D feature map.' The text also mentions ground truth dimensions of 256 (for SAM encoding) and 512 (for LSeg encoding), confirming the alignment with higher-dimensional targets.
